review: Disappointing Experience with Job… - Disappointing Experience with Job Nimbus - Limited Features and No Refund Policy. I recently had a less-than-pleasant experience with Job Nimbus, a CRM software that my company purchased based on their assurance that it would meet our needs. Unfortunately, our decision to trust their recommendation and bypass the free trial has proven to be a costly mistake. Within two weeks of making the annual upfront payment, we discovered that Job Nimbus lacked critical features essential to our business, notably the inability to generate a good, better, best quote—a fundamental requirement for our operations. This limitation, among others, severely hindered the software's functionality for our company. Upon realizing that Job Nimbus was not the solution we had hoped for, we promptly contacted the company requesting a refund for the unused months. Despite our genuine dissatisfaction and the fact that we had barely scratched the surface of their service, they declined to offer any refund. While I understand that terms and conditions may exist, it's disheartening to find out after the fact that we were expected to navigate through them diligently. We were not directed to review the terms and conditions during the purchasing process, which I believe is a lapse in communication and transparency on Job Nimbus's part. This lack of flexibility and understanding from Job Nimbus has left us not only with a software that doesn't meet our needs but also with a sense of frustration and disappointment in their customer service. It's disappointing to see a company prioritize their terms and conditions over customer satisfaction and goodwill. I hope this review serves as a cautionary tale for others considering Job Nimbus. I would strongly advise potential customers to thoroughly review the terms and conditions, and perhaps even reconsider using a company that is not willing to work with customers to find a satisfactory resolution. Transparency and customer-centric policies should be at the forefront of any business, and unfortunately, in our experience, Job Nimbus falls short in these aspects.
